newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest power mostly steady in normal temps.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest power mostly steady in normal temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady Tuesday as near normal temperatures moderated power demand, industry sources said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Wednesday peak, non-firm power prices were pegged steady at $16.50-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
MAPP temperatures were forecast to be seasonable to above normal through to Friday, then closer to normal levels through to the end of the week.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be unchanged at $11.00-13.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday were assessed steady at $16.50-17.50, the sources said.
Temperatures in MAIN were expected to be near normal Wednesday and Thursday, then cooling to near normal to five degrees below normal from Friday through the weekend.
MAIN off peak next day power was said to be steady at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.
In MAIN, Commonwealth Edison's 794 MW Dresden 3 nuclear power unit was holding at near 70 percent of capacity and was expected to reach full power later this week.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday were said to be discussed steady at 15.00-17.50, the sources said.
Temperatures in ECAR were expected to be near normal through Thursday.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm next day delivery were notionally assessed steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
March ECAR was said to be talked steady at $20.20-20.75 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were pegged higher at $17.50-19.50 in the north from $14.50-16.50 on Monday, while in the south next day peak power was assessed at $15.50-16.50 from $13.00-15.00 on Monday.
Off-peak non-firm next day prices throughout SPP were assessed higher at $10.50-12.50 from $10.00-12.00 on Monday.
In SPP, temperatures were forecast to be seasonable to just above normal to Thursday, then ease to normal levels Thursday and Friday.
March peak SPP was talked steady at $20.15-20.35 per MWh.
